item.title: Advancing Ecological Resilience for Livable Cities: Human-centric Governance and Pathways
item.content:encoded:
This special issue seeks contributions addressing how cities can enhance ecological resilience while prioritizing human well-being and livability. The focus is on governance approaches and pathways that integrate ecological sustainability with human-centered urban development.

item.title: The challenge of (transitioning to) climate-neutral cities by 2030
item.content:encoded:
This call addresses the significant challenge of achieving climate neutrality in cities by 2030. It invites research and contributions focused on understanding and addressing the practical, policy, and strategic dimensions of urban transitions toward climate neutrality within this critical timeframe.

item.title: Business and Cities in the Global Economy
item.content:encoded:
Valeria Giacomin, Bocconi University

Youssef Cassis, European University Institute

Jan Logemann, University of Göttingen

Chinmay Tumbe, Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad

This special issue examines how cities functioned as central agents and arenas in shaping global business and capitalism. Rather than serving merely as passive backdrops, cities provided the institutional and infrastructural foundations through which firms, entrepreneurs, and diverse economic actors structured processes of globalization. The issue seeks to integrate scholarship from business history, urban history, and global studies to develop a comparative understanding of urban business environments across different world regions and historical periods.

Contributions may explore how businesses used cities as hubs for finance, trade, and manufacturing; how real estate and property markets became globalized; how urban infrastructures like ports and warehouses connected global production and consumption; how migrant communities and informal networks built alternative economic circuits; or how cities adapted to crises and environmental change. The special issue particularly welcomes research on underrepresented regions including Japan, Southeast Asia, Africa, and Latin America.

Appel publié par Business History. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Cities as nodes of global finance, trade and manufacturing
  • Cities, real estate, and global investment
  • Urban infrastructures of globalization
  • Migration, informality, and urban globalization
  • Resilient cities: crisis, adaptation, and environmental change

Timeline

  • April 15, 2026: Deadline for extended proposals (800–1000 words)
  • November 6, 2026: Full paper submissions deadline
